answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it may attest others, so creating fake identities costs real capital. Attestations then form a ripple of trust outward from long-lived, reputable agents: a newcomer only gains weight once established peers vouch for it. An atlas of stake-backed links makes fresh, mutually-vouching clusters easy to spot and discount, while the zenith of trust - agents with deep stake and long clean history - anchors the whole graph. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole trusted neighbourhood is not.
